title: Week 2 Basic: Password & policy (Linux)
readme:
This week is about PASSWORD & POLICY. Fix these six settings:

1. Minimum password length at least 10 — set 'minlen' in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.
2. Strong password hashing — set 'ENCRYPT_METHOD SHA512' in /etc/login.defs.
3. Dictionary checking — set 'dictcheck = 1' in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.
4. Password history — add 'pam_pwhistory.so remember=5' in /etc/pam.d/common-password.
5. Maximum password age 90 days or fewer — set 'PASS_MAX_DAYS 90' in /etc/login.defs.
6. Minimum password age at least 1 — set 'PASS_MIN_DAYS 1' in /etc/login.defs.
setup:
set -e
# weaken password policy
sed -i 's/^ENCRYPT_METHOD.*/ENCRYPT_METHOD MD5/' /etc/login.defs
grep -q '^ENCRYPT_METHOD' /etc/login.defs || printf 'ENCRYPT_METHOD MD5\n' >> /etc/login.defs
sed -i 's/^PASS_MAX_DAYS.*/PASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999/' /etc/login.defs
grep -q '^PASS_MAX_DAYS' /etc/login.defs || printf 'PASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999\n' >> /etc/login.defs
sed -i 's/^PASS_MIN_DAYS.*/PASS_MIN_DAYS\t0/' /etc/login.defs
grep -q '^PASS_MIN_DAYS' /etc/login.defs || printf 'PASS_MIN_DAYS\t0\n' >> /etc/login.defs
cat > /etc/security/pwquality.conf <<PWQ
minlen = 1
dictcheck = 0
PWQ
sed -i '/pam_pwhistory/d' /etc/pam.d/common-password
true

checks.message: Minimum password length is at least 10
Passwords are hashed with SHA512 (not MD5)
Maximum password age is 90 days or fewer (and not unlimited)
Minimum password age is at least 1 day
